1) The estimated VTTC are different in different SC settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the value of time changes estimated from SC experiments is dependent on the design of the experiment.
the following question: how does the design of a stated choice (SC) experiment affect the estimated value of travel time savings (VTTC) and the covariates of a population?
the following question: “what are the effects of the SC experiment design on the estimated VTTC and covariate parameters?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SC design matters.
the SC setting matters, but the extent of the effects is difficult to predict.
the VTTC and its covariates are not constant across SC settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SC experiments should be designed to provide a wide range of VTTC estimates for a range of settings.
the SC design variables have an impact on the estimation of VTTC and covariate parameters.
the VTTC and other model estimates are not invariant to design variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VTTC and its covariates are not invariant to the SC setting.
the SC experiment should include all the relevant variables, and the levels should be carefully chosen so that they are not biased towards specific settings.
the SC experiment is not just a way to estimate the VTTC, but also to estimate a set of VTTC, which depends on the SC setting.
